## TL;DR

The round-one review identified a real grammar defect in the update/restart notice: active-work counts always used plural nouns. I changed the Vue copy to pluralize agent and check counts independently and added table-driven component coverage for (2,1), (1,2), (1,1), and (0,0). The Releases test file passes all 44 tests.

I then completed a second browser pass from the disposable scratch worktree on port 7278. It captured both chooser choices, pending and reloaded Notify/Publish states, cancellation, and a failed draft using an intercepted fake agent failure. The supervisor notice matrix includes hand-run, launchd, systemd, and uncertain detection at 1440 and 390 widths in light and dark. I inspected each final screenshot and attached all 24 captures to task #1168; screenshots remain out of git. No release was cut or published, and no real server was restarted. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final tracked tree.

## Work and rationale

The reviewer’s “1 checks” example came from a notice that interpolated counts but hardcoded both nouns as plural. I inspected the component and corrected each noun separately, because the counts can differ: one agent may be active while two checks run. The component test data now exercises independent singularization and zero-count wording. This is small UI copy logic, so the fix lives beside its existing component tests rather than introducing new formatting helpers.

The reviewer also questioned what “a correct command otherwise” means for supervised installs. I checked the existing notice behavior: launchd and systemd are presented with application actions, not shell commands; the uncertain detection state is the one that supplies an explicit manual command. I added a component test for this uncertain state, asserting the alert, exact scoped command, and absence of a Restart now button. An initial negative assertion rejected the phrase “Restart now” anywhere in the alert text, but that phrase is also used in explanatory copy about disruption. I narrowed it to the actual button label, which preserves the intended check without forbidding accurate descriptive text.

The QA record was rewritten after the reviewer pointed out discrepancies. It distinguishes the scratch worktree’s port 7278 evidence from earlier captures made at port 7371 in the task worktree, says that the hand-run message refers to recorded flags and port without showing their values, and names each actual screenshot. The final run uses `/releases?drawer=cut` to start from the intended state. It verified Notify’s wording does not imply publishing, that both pending requests survive reload, that their cancel controls clear the promises, and that the failed draft remains unpublished. The Playwright stub counted zero release mutation calls.

## Approaches tried

The first browser script tried to reach the cut panel by clicking its button and treated every POST to the notes endpoint as a new draft. Debugging showed that opening the panel performs a cached-only POST lookup as well. The script mistook that lookup for an actual Generate action, creating a false pending state that disabled the Generate button. The final harness recognizes the `cachedOnly` request and returns an empty cache result without starting a fake run. Starting at the documented deep-link route also avoids a click race and opens the panel directly.

The first cancellation click was intercepted by the open drawer overlay. The visible cancel button belonged to the server-owned pending banner behind that drawer. The final script dispatches a click on the button element itself and waits for the stubbed DELETE to clear the pending record. With those harness corrections, the browser pass completed and produced the intended screenshots. Each screenshot was opened and inspected after waiting for the theme and dialog transitions, including all dark mode restart captures.

## Challenges and blockers

This task crosses user-facing release behavior and service restart behavior, so the browser setup had to guarantee that no irreversible action reached the server. Playwright intercepted all relevant API calls. The release cut/publish route was guarded by a mutation counter that stayed at zero, and the restart notice buttons were never clicked. The fake failed-draft response tested the error state without launching an agent. launchd and systemd were represented through fixture-shaped update-status responses on the macOS host rather than real service managers.

The first full check caught an over-broad assertion in the new uncertain-supervisor test, and a later run found formatting differences in the Vue and test files. I corrected the assertion, ran the formatter, and reran the full scoped check. Remote validation completed the build, scoped suite (173 tests), and UI smoke; local format, lint, build freshness, rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke all passed. The generated report draft remains in the ignored engineering-report directory for RepoOS to finalize against the checked tree.

## Key learnings

A test fixture with two agents and one check reveals grammar defects that symmetric counts can hide. UI assertions should target the control that matters rather than ban a phrase that is also valid in explanatory copy. Browser request stubs must preserve distinctions between read-only cache lookup and user-triggered generation, or the test harness can manufacture exactly the disabled state it is meant to investigate. For screenshot QA, provenance matters: worktree, port, theme transition settling, and the state encoded by each filename should all agree with the evidence attached to the task.
